meta.title: AI context
meta.description: How to give a coding agent the complete React Scheduler documentation in one file, and how to check that it read it.

prerequisites.text: An agentic coding tool — Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or another — with your repository open. Nothing is installed for this: it is one Markdown file and one line of instruction.

install.download: Download the documentation into your repository:
install.instruction: Then add one line to the file your tool reads on every session — CLAUDE.md for Claude Code, AGENTS.md for Codex, Cursor and most others:
install.url: A tool that indexes documentation by URL can be given https://react-schedulerkit.vercel.app/react-scheduler/llms-full.md instead of a local copy. Re-download it when you upgrade the package: the file is generated in the same build as this site, so the two can never disagree.

what.text: Every page of this site, in reading order, as one Markdown document:
points: the prose of each page, with its headings and tables;
the full source of every live example, exactly as it runs here;
the API reference, generated from the package's own type declarations — every prop, its type, its default and its description.

rows: Every page and every example, as Markdown
Your tool reads Markdown and the context window can hold it
The same content as plain text
A link index: every page, with its one-line description
The full file is too large, or the tool fetches pages on demand
You know which page answers the question
which.context: The full file is around 240 kB, which fits in current models but crowds a small context window. If yours is tight, give the agent llms.txt and let it fetch the one page it needs — every page of this site is reachable by appending .md to its URL.

example.text: One prompt that uses the file. The agent has the props, the defaults and the examples, so it does not have to guess an API:

verify.text: Ask a question only the documentation answers. If the agent invents a plausible prop name, it did not read the file:
verify.answer: The answer is overflowMergeWindow: consecutive hours merge into one group only while the merged group stays inside that window. It is on the Timeline view page.
